site.name: Irene Mine
site.location: Boulder County Tungsten Mining District, north of Nederland
overview: The Irene Mine was a documented tungsten producer in Boulder County's tungsten district, about nine miles north of Nederland.

Colorado Geological Survey records describe a 150-foot shaft with two levels and an adit connecting to the 70-foot level, while USGS MRDS preserves a mine-level location for the Irene tungsten producer.

timeline.text: The Irene property was developed with a 150-foot shaft, two levels, and an adit that joined the 70-foot level.
Colorado Geological Survey records report production of five tons of ore averaging 0.89 percent tungsten oxide.
The property was recorded under owner and last operator J. E. Spaulding, with horn ore reported locally as running up to about 3 percent tungsten oxide.

moreHistory: Colorado Geological Survey MI-04 places Irene in the northeast quarter of Section 31, Township 1 North, Range 72 West, south of the Washington Avenue Mine and roughly nine miles north of Nederland.
The same survey records the mine's shaft-and-adit workings, limited 1955 production, and a vein exposed at the surface by bulldozer work.

USGS Mineral Resources Data System record 10108233 identifies Irene as a Boulder County tungsten producer at approximately 40.00666, -105.49226. Remnant uses that published mine-level coordinate as the identification anchor and does not claim that it is a field-surveyed surviving shaft collar.
